analysis.title: Hot CPI, Hawkish Fed, Shrugging Tape: Top Goldman Trader Says Hedged-To-The-Gills Funds Are Propping Up Stocks
key_insights: Goldman's Privorotsky had said core CPI at 0.2% would be constructive and 0.3% would challenge the rally. Core printed 0.3% and SPX barely fell, with futures recovering the next morning.

CPI was hot across the board: headline +0.4%, core +0.3% vs 0.3% and 0.2% expected. Strength extended beyond energy into medical services and insurance. Goldman's economists had penciled in core of about +0.16%.

Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered in December if core came in around 0.3% or higher, and Logan added hawkish comments. Markets now price a December hike with some optionality of 50bp, and about three hikes through the end of 2027.

The 2Y yield spiked about 20bp at its worst, the biggest move since Liberation Day. The 10Y moved back above 5% after a weak auction (tail), and the 2s30s curve flattened about 9bps in one session (bear flattening). Goldman economists added a third hike.
VIX briefly traded into the 20s but finished below 20, and vol sellers returned quickly. Privorotsky says positioning may now be doing more to support the tape than macro is doing to undermine it.

Hedge fund net exposure hit 5-year lows after what Privorotsky called one of the most aggressive episodes of net/gross de-risking in the US prime book in a decade. Funds are heavily hedged, so a bad print has fewer sellers left.

Under the surface the tape was weaker: Nasdaq and Russell led the losses, Nvidia is down about $2 trillion from its highs, Goldman estimates CTAs will sell about $31B of S&P futures over the next week, and high yield led credit wider. Privorotsky flags credit as the one to watch.

On AI, Privorotsky says sentiment is improving and overnight neocloud commentary was broadly supportive, with data center capacity the main bottleneck and compute utilization elevated. The article notes CoreWeave beat and raised but guided to a $1.1B quarterly interest bill, with debt at $47B, record Q3 cash burn of $7.5B and unsecured bonds yielding over 15%.

Oil: Rubio's post-G7 remarks suggest Washington favors sustained economic pressure and the naval blockade over resuming major combat operations. Qatari mediators are working in an estimated two-week window. Brent briefly broke below $90 for the first time since August. Privorotsky says directional conviction is low, and if Brent consolidates near $90 with falling realized vol, equities should look through the headlines.

Privorotsky frames the risk as positioning being a tailwind and the Fed a headwind. He says yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem for equities, and notes reflexivity between energy, inflation and the Fed.

The ZeroHedge author disputes the energy-pass-through view: strength was in medical services and insurance, not gasoline, and Goldman economists see larger start-of-year price increases pushing a third hike into 2027. The author argues positioning can delay but rarely overturns the Fed's verdict, and flags the December FOMC as the next catalyst.
Bond market closed Veterans Day while equities were open. Privorotsky is watching neoclouds and the next move in energy.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge fund nets are at 5-year lows and funds are heavily hedged, so few sellers remain. Vol sellers keep returning and the volatility premium should decay absent fresh negative information (Goldman's Privorotsky).
tension_points.bear_case: CPI strength was in medical services and insurance rather than energy, Goldman economists see a third hike in 2027, the 10Y is above 5% and high yield is leading credit wider (ZeroHedge author).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields making another leg higher, which Privorotsky says would become a material problem for equities, or a VIX break above 20 on a data point such as the December FOMC.

tension_points.bull_case: If Brent consolidates near $90 with collapsing realized volatility, equities should look through headline noise. The US favors economic pressure over combat.
tension_points.bear_case: The two-week Qatari mediation window is unconfirmed and fluid, Iran is moving missile production underground, and the pattern of Monday de-escalation and Friday re-escalation could repeat.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brent consolidating near $90 with collapsing realized volatility would support the bull case. A return to major combat operations would break it.
